well: IODP Holes 375-U1520C and 375-U1520D - HIKURANGI TROUGH subduction inputs, offshore North Island, New Zealand (38.969 S, 179.132 E; seafloors -3,522.1 / -3,531.5 m), 15 km east of the plate boundary that hosts the world's best-documented SHALLOW SLOW SLIP EVENTS (<15 km); Expedition 375 (2018), samples 477.00-1036.50 mbsf spanning the subducting sedimentary sequence that BECOMES the SSE fault once carried into the subduction zone
operator_on_log: Eijsink & Ikari (MARUM) laboratory shearing experiments at plate-rate to SSE-rate velocities under IN-SITU effective normal stress; drilling by JOIDES Resolution; the catalogue's third Ikari-lab entry (companion to the Nankai strength table and the JFAST Tohoku slow-slip table)
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.942335 ('Frictional data for the experiments performed under in-situ effective normal stress of samples from IODP Site 375-U1520'), child 1 of bundle doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.942371; supplement to Eijsink & Ikari 2022, G-cubed 23(6), e2022GC010369 (doi:10.1029/2022GC010369)
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0), declared IN the file's own header; Curation Level: Enhanced curation. Attribution: Eijsink/Ikari / PANGAEA / IODP
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (466 data points per the header's own Size declaration = 490 non-empty body cells minus the Event-label and geocode-depth columns, re-counted at gate time) in one fetch. DISCLOSURE: the bundle's sibling dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.942341 (per-event slip statistics, 5,246 points) EXCEEDS this environment's fetch size cap and was left OUT rather than archived incomplete - the complete-dataset rule outranks the wish to have it
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 12 laboratory friction experiments on the six major U1520 lithologies (III siltstone, IV calcareous mudstone/chalk/marl, V volcaniclastics incl. red-cement and zeolite variants, VI black layer / blue volcaniclastics; intact and powdered), sheared at in-situ effective normal stress 3,995-9,384 kPa: peak/steady-state/final friction coefficients (0.248-0.740 span), velocity-dependent (a-b) with std dev, critical stiffnesses with k/kc ratios, and full forward + inverse rate-state model parameter sets (a, b1, b2, dc1, dc2, machine stiffness, each with inverse-model std devs)
curves: a-b + std dev (velocity dependence - the SSE-capability parameter)
forward-model µ0, a, b1, b2, dc1, dc2, k
inverse-model µ0, a, b1, b2, dc1, dc2, k each with std dev ('not inverted' rows carried verbatim)
Event rides as per-sample quality; Exp/Sample label/Description/Samp type verbatim in file
source_anomaly_disclosure: THREE source quirks preserved verbatim: (1) COLUMN-LABEL SWAP - the header declares the stiffness quartet in order (kc, k/kc, kb, k/kb) but the data carries (kc, kb, k/kc, k/kb): re-deriving k/column-14 reproduces column 16 and k/column-15 reproduces column 17 on ALL 11 modeled rows to <=3e-5 relative (including AE38's negative kc: 9331.34/-44.667 = -208.91), so two adjacent labels are transposed in the archive header - detected by arithmetic, carried unchanged; (2) experiment AE27's ID contains an embedded space ('AE27_U1520C37R1p _SST') and its sample label is truncated to '375-U1520C-37'; (3) the AE25 chalk-powder row carries only 13 of 46 cells - it is the same experiment recorded as 'no SSEs with significant peak (or drop) in velocity' in the bundle's statistics sibling, its refusal preserved here as a nearly-empty row
purpose: thirty-second catalogue entry - the HIKURANGI MARGIN joins as region TWENTY and rate-state friction parameters are kind TWENTY-ONE: where entry 31 (JFAST) archives laboratory slow slip events on the fault that ALREADY ruptured (Tohoku 2011), this entry archives the frictional constitution of sediments BEFORE subduction - which lithologies CAN host slow slip - and the paper's headline closes the pair: every carbonate row (chalk, calcareous mudstone, marl) is velocity-WEAKENING (a-b < 0, SSE-capable) while the black layer and blue volcaniclastics are velocity-strengthening (stable creep); this file also drove the read_pangaea_txt duplicate-channel-name upgrade - its triple 'k [kPa/mm]' and doubled µ0/a/b1/b2/dc1/dc2 columns silently overwrote each other in the pre-upgrade reader
verified: 466 non-empty counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (excluding Event label + geocode depth columns, EXACT); k/kc column-swap arithmetic re-derived on all 11 modeled rows (worst 3e-5 relative); all 5 carbonate rows velocity-weakening and all 3 strengthening rows non-carbonate (paper's lithology-control headline); SigmaN strictly increasing across all 9 unique depths (477->3,995 kPa to 1,036.5->9,384 kPa); peak > steady-state friction on all 12 rows; AE25 sparse-row cross-link pinned; duplicate-channel dedupe verified to change ZERO existing entries; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
